title: B2B sales intelligence platforms: what repeat CRM exports and refreshes cost
summary: Compare UpLead, Lusha and Cognism rules for repeat exports, changed CRM rows and data refreshes before buying a B2B sales intelligence platform.
body_markdown:
A contact already paid for can still generate another charge when your team exports it, pushes an update to the CRM, or requests changed details. Which action triggers that charge depends on the platform and the part of the product you use.


For a RevOps buyer, the useful comparison is not just how many contacts a subscription includes. It is what happens when the same records pass through your workflow again.


We compared public pricing pages and product documentation on November 23, 2026; we did not test data accuracy or live CRM sync.


## Compare the action, not just the credit allowance


Ask vendors to price the same sequence: reveal a contact, export it, send it to your CRM, then handle that record again after its details change. A credit allowance alone does not tell you the cost of that sequence.


Action


UpLead


Lusha


Cognism


Reveal contact details for the first time


One credit unlocks a contact’s full details, including email, phone and mobile.[Credit rules](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


In Platform and Extension, an email costs one credit; a phone number costs five; email plus phone can cost up to six.[Credit rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


One credit reveals one contact.[Pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


View details already revealed


Unlocked records are available in Downloads.[Credit rules](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


Re-viewing already revealed details costs zero credits in Platform and Extension.[Credit rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


Previously revealed contacts can be viewed without another charge, with continued use of redeemed records throughout the contract.[Pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


Export the records again


Repeat downloads or exports of unlocked records **from Downloads** are free.[Credit rules](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


**Workspace CSV export** costs one credit per 25 rows, separately from reveal charges.[Credit rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


Ask the vendor to demonstrate the credit treatment for your repeat-export route.


Push rows to the CRM


First export of a previously locked record uses a credit; repeat exports from Downloads do not. Confirm the rules for your intended integration and plan.[Credit rules](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


**Workspace pushes to Salesforce or HubSpot** cost one credit per changed row. Rows already matching the CRM are not charged.[Credit rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


Ask which CRM Enrichment package and credit rules apply to the proposed workflow.


Maintain data after details change


Free Downloads exports do not establish a fresh-data or maintenance entitlement.


Workspace AI data enrichment costs one credit per cell; CRM delivery has its own changed-row rule.[Credit rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


CRM Enrichment includes ongoing maintenance, but credits are used again when key details change, such as a job move.[Pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


The last two rows deserve separate attention. Finding a changed value and writing that value into a CRM are different operations. Have the vendor identify the charge for each operation rather than describe the whole workflow as “enrichment.”


## UpLead: free repeat exports from Downloads, not a promise of refreshed records


UpLead’s documented reuse rule is straightforward: once a record is unlocked and in Downloads, exporting or downloading it again from that list is free. An initial export consumes a credit only if the record has not already been unlocked. Unlocking a contact’s full details costs one credit; unlocking previously locked company data also costs one credit.[Source: UpLead credit documentation](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


That makes UpLead worth considering when your repeat task is retrieving records you have already purchased. Preserve the distinction between retrieving those records and obtaining current information about them. The Downloads rule establishes free repeat delivery, not an entitlement to refreshed data.


The subscription also needs to fit the people and integrations involved. UpLead lists monthly Essentials at $99 with 170 monthly credits and Plus at $199 with 400 monthly credits. Both are single-user plans. Annual billing is advertised at an effective $74 per month with 2,040 annual credits for Essentials, and $149 per month with 4,800 annual credits for Plus. Professional is a custom-priced annual team account.[Source: UpLead pricing](https://www.uplead.com/pricing/)


Plus lists data enrichment, while Professional lists bidirectional CRM integration and full API access. For a repeated CRM workflow, ask which plan supports the exact connection you intend to use and what happens when an already-unlocked contact changes jobs.[Source: UpLead pricing](https://www.uplead.com/pricing/)


Have the vendor export an unlocked record from Downloads, then show how that same record receives updated information. Treat those as separate demonstrations.


## Lusha: free viewing does not mean free Workspace delivery


Lusha separates the price of revealing data from the price of moving it through Workspace.


In Platform and Extension, revealing an email costs one credit and revealing a phone number costs five. Email plus phone can therefore cost up to six credits. Re-viewing already revealed details costs zero credits. Workspace CSV exports, however, cost one credit per 25 rows, separately from the reveal charge.[Source: Lusha credit documentation](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


This matters if users regularly reopen a saved list and send it elsewhere. The zero-credit viewing rule does not answer what a Workspace CSV export costs. Nor should the Workspace rule be applied to every export route in every Lusha product.


For Workspace CRM pushes to Salesforce or HubSpot, the billing unit changes again: one credit per **changed row** , not per export job. A row already matching the CRM is not charged. Lusha’s own worked example describes 500 rows with 50 changed rows, producing a charge of 50 credits.[Source: Lusha credit documentation](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


Ask what counts as a changed row in your configuration. You need to see the field mapping, the values compared and the resulting credit deduction. A successful sync alone does not show whether the billing matches your expected maintenance workload.


Workspace AI data enrichment uses another unit: one credit per cell. Signals cost one credit per signal detected, and the same signal in two tables incurs separate charges. A Workspace signal search with no signal detected costs zero credits.[Source: Lusha credit documentation](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


API rules also differ from the interface. For example, company information is free in Platform but costs a credit through the API, where additional request costs and a minimum charge for no-result requests can apply. An API-led workflow therefore needs its own quote rather than a cost estimate copied from the Platform rules.[Source: Lusha credit documentation](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


Run the same saved records through the Workspace CSV route and the CRM push route. Inspect the ledger after each operation, including a repeat CRM push with unchanged rows.


## Cognism: maintenance is included, but changed details can consume credits again


Cognism explicitly addresses ongoing CRM maintenance. Its pricing page says CRM Enrichment is available as a standalone product or an add-on, with ongoing maintenance included. It also says credits are used again when key details change, such as when a contact moves jobs.[Source: Cognism pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


That is a more useful description for a maintenance buyer than a promise of access to previously revealed contacts. It still requires a budget for changes.


For contact access, Cognism states that one credit reveals one contact, previously revealed contacts can be viewed without another charge, and redeemed records remain available for continued use throughout the contract. A job change can trigger another credit.[Source: Cognism pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


The purchase question is therefore which changes consume credits and how those changes reach your CRM. Ask the vendor to distinguish a record that remains unchanged from one whose key details have changed. Then ask how each appears in the activity log and credit ledger.


Standard and Pro both list five included seats, with pricing supplied by quote. The quote should identify whether CRM Enrichment is included in the proposed package or purchased separately, as well as the allowance available for changed records.[Source: Cognism pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)


Follow an already-redeemed contact through a job-change update. Get the update frequency, charge trigger and CRM write behavior documented alongside the quote.


## Apollo: confirm action charges inside the proposed account


For Apollo, check the credit pool and its expiry terms before treating unused capacity as a reserve for future CRM work. Its pricing page describes shared team credits supplied upfront for the billing cycle. Unused credits, including add-on credits, expire. Credit add-ons recur until removed before renewal, and all seats must use the same plan.[Source: Apollo pricing](https://www.apollo.io/pricing)


Have the vendor show the in-account charges for your reveal, repeat-export and refresh actions, then attach those rules to the quote. The public terms cited here do not settle those individual workflow costs.


If the intended use supplies data to a customer-facing product, raise that before purchasing. Apollo’s standard terms cover internal business use; customer-facing products require a separate agreement.[Source: Apollo pricing](https://www.apollo.io/pricing)


For Apollo-specific subscription terms, see our[Apollo pricing guide](https://coldreach.ai/blog/apollo-pricing) . For a broader vendor shortlist, compare[ZoomInfo alternatives](https://coldreach.ai/blog/zoominfo-alternatives) .


## A vendor demo checklist for repeated CRM use


Bring a small set of records your team is authorized to process. Include already-revealed contacts, CRM rows with matching values and records with known changes. Ask the vendor to use the proposed plan and integration, not a different product surface.


1.


Record the starting balance. Capture the plan, available credits, billing cycle and any separate credit pools. Ask which balance each operation will use.


2.


Reveal a new contact. Request the fields your team actually needs. Check whether the charge is per contact, email, phone number or field.


3.


Export the revealed record twice through the intended route. Specify Downloads, Workspace CSV, a CRM connector or an API. Capture both deductions rather than accepting “already purchased” as the answer.


4.


Push matching rows to the CRM. Inspect the sync log and ledger. For Lusha Workspace, confirm that rows already matching Salesforce or HubSpot are not charged.


5.


Process changed records separately. Ask which fields trigger a charge, whether the unit is a row or a cell, and whether detecting the change and delivering it consume separate credits.


6.


Follow a job change. Have the vendor show what happens to the original record, the new company association and the CRM fields. For Cognism, confirm when the additional credit is redeemed.


7.


Document the maintenance schedule and contract terms. Get the refresh frequency, write permissions, treatment of manual CRM edits, credit expiry and recurring add-ons in writing.


Keep the resulting action log with the quote. It gives finance and RevOps something more useful to review than a total credit allowance.


## FAQ


### Does exporting the same contact again always use another credit?


No. UpLead documents free repeat downloads and exports of unlocked records from Downloads. Lusha Workspace separately charges one credit per 25 rows for CSV exports. The answer depends on the export route, not just whether the contact was previously revealed.[UpLead rules](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit) ,[Lusha rules](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


### Does a free repeat export include fresh contact data?


Not by itself. UpLead’s documented Downloads rule covers exporting an unlocked record again; it does not establish an ongoing refresh entitlement. Ask the vendor to show how changed details are obtained, how often that happens and whether obtaining them consumes credits.[Source: UpLead credit documentation](https://support.uplead.com/en/articles/5621272-what-is-a-credit)


### Does Lusha charge for every row sent to Salesforce or HubSpot?


For Workspace CRM pushes, Lusha says it charges one credit per changed row. Rows already matching the CRM are not charged. Its published example is 500 rows with 50 changed rows, costing 50 credits. That is a different rule from Workspace CSV export pricing.[Source: Lusha credit documentation](https://docs.lusha.com/user-guide/getting-started/how-credits-work-in-lusha)


### Does Cognism’s included CRM maintenance mean updates never consume credits?


No. Cognism says ongoing CRM maintenance is included, but credits are used again when key details change, such as a job move. Ask the vendor to document which changes trigger another credit and which CRM Enrichment package is included in your quote.[Source: Cognism pricing](https://www.cognism.com/pricing)
